title: Daughter of the Rock
teaser: Granite hills, blue tourmaline, and a letter that turns Nabyen's whole life upside down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Jos, Plateau State. Morning sun on the granite hills, and air cool enough to make Lagos jealous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop had a tray of blue tourmaline in one hand and a customer haggling in her ear when the boy came running.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Slow down, Dung! Who is chasing you?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He pressed an envelope into her hands. Red wax, stamped with two rivers meeting.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.text: Nabyen. If you are reading this, I am gone. Come to Port Harcourt. Trust the rivers, not the men who sail them. — G.O.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pressed flat inside the envelope: a single red rose petal. Like the rose on her windowsill.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Chief Gideon Okoro? THE Chief Gideon? Why would a man like that write to me?

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: Give me that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her mother's hands were shaking.

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: Not here. Not in front of the whole market. Tonight, at the rocks.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Kaneng folds the letter into her wrapper the way you fold away a prayer. Her eyes are wet.

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: Close the stall early, my daughter. We need to talk.

choices.text: Drop the letter in the brazier. Rich men's problems are not hers.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: The wax hisses. Kaneng snatches the letter out of the coals with her bare hand.

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: This IS your problem. It has been your problem since before you were born.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, there is a note tucked into the frame of her front door. Cream paper. Old-fashioned handwriting, the kind nobody learns any more.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: You don't know me yet. But I have known you all your life. Don't go to Port Harcourt alone. — W.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the street, under the jacaranda, something moves in the dark. When she looks properly, there is nobody there.

scenes.prompt: The note smells faintly of the river.

choices.text: Burn it. Nobody watches a Dalyop woman.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: The paper curls in the flame. The ink, strangely, doesn't burn. The letter W glows for a moment, then the ash blows away.

choices.text: Keep it. Sleep with it under her pillow.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She tells herself it's so she won't lose the evidence. She doesn't believe herself.

choices.text: Write a reply and leave it on the step: "Then show yourself."

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: In the morning, her note is gone. In its place, a red rose, still wet with dew.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Evening at the balancing rocks. The sky goes orange, then violet, then full of stars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mama Kaneng brings out a bundle wrapped in faded ankara. Inside, a leather diary, its pages brown with age.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: Your grandmother's. Nana Rinji. She could see things. I never wanted you to read this.

lines.speaker: diary
lines.text: The women of our line see the river before a death. My mother saw it. I saw it. Forgive me, child: you will see it too.

lines.speaker: diary
lines.text: When the coral is broken, the family is broken. When the two halves meet, the river will choose, and the dead will rest.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Mama. Last night I dreamed of a river.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: ...I know. So did I.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: Thirty years ago, a young man came up from the river to buy tin. Tall. Loud. He laughed like thunder.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: He stayed one rainy season. Then his father called him home to build an empire, and he went.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: He sent money every year. I sent it back every year. Pride is a heavy wrapper to wear, Nabyen.

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: Was. Is. Blood doesn't care about funerals.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She presses half a coral bracelet into Nabyen's palm. "He kept the other half. Every day of his life."

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: Because men with empires have enemies, and I wanted you to have a life, not a crown.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She presses half a coral bracelet into Nabyen's palm. "He kept the other half."

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: Of course you are. You are his daughter as much as mine.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She presses half a coral bracelet into Nabyen's palm. "Take this. He has the other half."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next morning the market is louder than usual, because a black SUV with Lagos plates is parked in the middle of it.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop. Kolade Balogun, House of the Lagoon. I flew up at dawn just to meet you.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: We got the same letter. Mine said 'earn it.' I'm guessing yours said something kinder.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: I have a jet waiting at Heipang. Port Harcourt by lunch. We could be allies, you and I.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then her phone buzzes. A voice she hasn't heard since she was twelve and learning to swim in the creeks.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: Nabyen? It's Tari. Tari Ebiowei. The Chief asked me to keep you safe. Don't get in any car from Lagos.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Smart woman. Lagos and the Plateau. Together we'd be unstoppable.

choices.text: Tell Tari to come and get her.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: Take the bus to Makurdi. I'll meet you at the river. I'm already on my way.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Suit yourself. I'll save you a seat at the table.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: I carry my own stones down the hill, Mr Balogun. I can carry myself to Port Harcourt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As the road climbs out of Jos, Nabyen looks back. The sky over Terminus market is glowing orange.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her stall. Her mother's stall. Thirty years of it, burning.

lines.speaker: phone
lines.text: That was a warning, Miss Dalyop. The next one won't be.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Whoever you are, you just made the worst mistake of your life.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The jet hums south over the dark Benue. Kolade sleeps. Nabyen doesn't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bus rattles south through the night, past dark hills and sleeping towns.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: I saw the fire. I am sorry about your mother's stall. I will not let them touch you. — W.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: You wrote back. Nobody has ever written back. I will show myself when it is safe, I promise. — W.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She opens her bag for water and finds something that wasn't there this morning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A business card. Heavy cream paper. 'Banque Moreau, Genève.' On the back, in neat handwriting: 'Stay in Jos.'

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Someone was in my room.

scenes.prompt: Somebody wants her to stay home.

choices.text: Keep the card hidden. Whoever sent it is watching.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Moreau. I'll remember you.

choices.text: Tear it in half. She doesn't take orders from strangers.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She keeps the half with the name on it, though. She's angry, not foolish.

outcomes.title: Wings over the Benue
outcomes.text: Nabyen flew south with Lagos at her side. Kolade is charming, generous and very interested in her future. Maybe a little too interested.

outcomes.title: The River Remembers
outcomes.text: Nabyen called the boy who taught her to swim. He came at once, the way rivers do.

outcomes.title: Her Own Road
outcomes.text: Nabyen went south alone, owing nobody anything. In a game of thrones, that's rare and dangerous.

reflections.text: Someone out there has your handwriting now.
Mama Kaneng's hand is bandaged. She hasn't mentioned it.
Nabyen knows who her father was. Soon everyone else will too.

s_plea.title: A father's plea
s_plea.text: PLEA, hidden in the Plateau. On the back of the Chief's letter, in pencil so faint she almost missed it: 'Forgive me, Kaneng.'

m_jos.title: Morning on the Rocks
m_jos.text: Blue tourmaline, cool air, and a boy running with a red-wax letter.

m_road.title: The Road South
m_road.text: A card that says 'Stay in Jos.' She didn't.

k_bracelet.title: Half a coral bracelet
k_bracelet.text: Warm from Mama's hand. The break is clean, as if someone always meant to mend it.

k_card.title: A cream business card
k_card.text: 'Stay in Jos.' Neat handwriting. A woman's, she thinks.

k_diary.title: Nana Rinji's diary
k_diary.text: "When the coral is broken, the family is broken. When the two halves meet, the river will choose."

epigraph.text: The women of the Rock see the river before a death.
